The retainer looks like this:

The event listener captures the `LView` for `BComponent` in Ivy's `instructionState.lFrame.contextLView`, which is apparently never cleared.

body:
I'm looking forward to resolving this issue :)

For those who faced this problem replacing `*ngIf` with `[hidden]` might be a temporary solution
@s3141p the leak would occur for _any_ embedded view though, so you'd also see this inside of `ngFor` for example.

I decided to give the proposal from @petebacondarwin a quick try, but it ended up breaking a bunch of event listener tests so we may need to do something more sophisticated. Here's the code for reference: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a11c156292f230e9d2dfa8be64a59c10e9e45c3f

I think `leaveView` is not the correct call; that pops an `LFrame` from the instruction stack whereas `restoreView` never pushed a frame, so the stack ends up being inconsistent. The `contextLView` that is set in `restoreView` is set on the currently active frame, which I think would typically be the root frame. Clearing `contextLView` on that frame should be sufficient to avoid the memory leak.

issue.body:
When we have an event listener inside an embedded view, we generate a `restoreView` call which saves the view inside of the LFrame. The problem is that we don't clear it until it gets overwritten which can lead to memory leaks.

These changes rework the generated code in order to generate a `resetView` call which will clear the view from the LFrame.

Fixes #42848.
